newsitem.title: GERMANY: France's Giscard suggests forum for EMU talks.
newsitem.headline: France's Giscard suggests forum for EMU talks.

text.p: Former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing suggested on Saturday a so-called European currency committee may be worth creating as the number of nations joining currency union will be limited at first.

In an opinion piece published in Saturday's Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Giscard d'Estaing said Europe's future central bank would benefit from a forum where European and national monetary policies could be discussed.
"At least at the beginning, only a limited number of states will be able to join the currency union," he said, adding "Why shouldn't we investigate the idea of a European currency committee."
This would give all relevant policy makers a chance to discuss important issues, he said.
But he also stressed that the future European central bank should be independent of any political influences.
"There can be no counterweight group which can force its will on the European central bank," he said.
Europe's currency union is scheduled to begin 1999 with all the nations meeting strict entry criteria.
